correctness.rationale: At degree j, conjugation by t+c t^j preserves every lower coefficient and shifts the degree-j coefficient by c(a^j-a). Retain each eliminated coefficient just before elimination as an auxiliary coordinate; it and each retained resonant coordinate are affine bijections of the original coefficient at that degree, for every choice of earlier ones. This proves the uniform product law on the resonant coefficients, not a law on conjugacy classes. The resonance degrees sd+1 have 1≤s≤m−1. All nonzero exponent residues modulo d have invertible substitution-minus-identity by the diagonal entries. On the zero residue algebra z=t^d, first resonance r gives a nonzero term γ z^(r+1), with γ=d b_r, in φ(z)-z. A first nonconstant term u_j z^j in an invariant would change by jγu_j z^(j+r) if j+r≤m; no higher term can cancel this, and j≤m−r<p, including m=p. All remaining monomials are individually fixed, with multiplication inherited from the truncated z-ring, or the whole z-ring is fixed when all coefficients vanish. Thus this is an algebra classification, and the independent coordinates give the stated first-hit law and its dimension expectation. The argument includes d=1 with no eliminations. Independently enumerating fixed vectors directly over F2 and F3 on three in-range cases gave the expected dimension counts, with the out-of-range p=2,m=3 counts {3:3,4:1} (/workspace/replay/independent_checks.py, fixed). That finite replay is not a proof or an arbitrary-field multiplication certificate.
